outcomes.text: Understand and respond to texts written in Urdu, drawn from a variety of sources such as magazines, newspapers, reports, books and other forms of extended writing.
Manipulate Urdu accurately in spoken and written forms, choosing appropriate examples of lexis and structures.
Select information and present it in Urdu.
Organise arguments and ideas logically.
Know that all textual material used in the examinations is drawn from the topic areas, with reference to the country or countries where Urdu is spoken.
Topic areas: Human relationships; Family; Generation gap; Young people; Patterns of daily life; Urban and rural life; The media.
Topic areas: Food and drink; Law and order; Philosophy and belief; Health and fitness; Work and leisure; Equality of opportunity; Employment and unemployment.
Topic areas: Sport; Free time activities; Travel and tourism; Education; Cultural life/heritage; War and peace; Social and economic development.
Topic areas: Scientific and medical advances; Technological innovation; Environment; Conservation; Pollution; Contemporary aspects of the country or countries where Urdu is spoken.

Read two passages in Urdu dealing with related themes (together not exceeding 750 words, written during the last twenty years and reflecting the international scene), using Urdu for all questions and answers.
On the first passage, answer two tests (5 marks each) covering vocabulary recognition and grammatical manipulation.
On the first passage, answer a series of comprehension questions (15 marks for Content and 5 marks for Quality of Language).
On the second passage, answer a series of comprehension questions (15 marks for Content and 5 marks for Quality of Language).

Write about 140 words drawing information from both passages and adding your own opinions, as a summary or comparison of issues raised (10 marks for information from the passages, 5 for personal response, 5 for Quality of Language).
Choose one of five questions, one set on each of the five set topics, and write an essay in Urdu of 250–400 words.
Know that of the 40 marks, 24 are for the quality of the language and 16 for the content.
Set topics for examination in 2025: 1. Human relationships; 2. Philosophy and belief; 3. Work and leisure; 4. Education; 5. Conservation.
Set topics for examination in 2026: 1. Generation gap; 2. The media; 3. Employment and unemployment; 4. Free time activities; 5. Social and economic development.

topics.title: Human relationships – family – generation gap – young people

outcomes.text: Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): family activities; new patterns of family relationships; the status of the elderly and responsibility for their care.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): generation gap; conflicts in the family circle; young people and the older generation; attitudes of young people to the family environment.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): young people; young people and their peer group; young people as a target group for advertisers and politicians.

topics.title: Patterns of daily life – urban and rural life – the media – food and drink – law and order – philosophy and belief – health and fitness

outcomes.text: Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): daily routine; school; the individual’s way of life; living conditions.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): advantages and disadvantages of urban and rural life; transport and communications; shopping; housing.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): the role and influence of the media; the power of advertising.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): healthy eating; fast-food; national traditions of eating and drinking.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): violence and crime; drug-related crime; the role of the police; law-enforcement.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): the role of philosophy and belief in a local, national and an international context; attitudes towards different beliefs and philosophical issues; philosophical and religious practices/groups; values and morality.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): healthy living; exercise; dieting; drugs; health care provision; stress; AIDS.

topics.title: Work and leisure – equality of opportunity – employment and unemployment – sport – free time activities – travel and tourism – education – cultural life/heritage

outcomes.text: Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): women in society and in the workforce; equality of opportunity for minority groups.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): preparation for work and job opportunities; career plans; qualifications and job routines; plight of the unemployed, areas of high unemployment; demise of traditional industries; possible solutions, immigrant workers.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): individual and team sports; amateur and professional sport.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): value of leisure; balance between leisure and work; planning leisure time.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): tourism as a modern phenomenon; friction between tourists and local inhabitants; holidays and foreign travel.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): education systems and types of school; patterns of curriculum; relationship between education and training; further and higher education provision; examinations.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): the world of the arts; significant figures and trends in the arts; the place of culture and the arts in the life of the nation.

topics.title: War and peace – social and economic development

outcomes.text: Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): conflicts in the world: ethnic, religious, ideological.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): positive and negative aspects of social and economic development; recent and predicted trends.

topics.title: Medical advances – scientific and technological innovation

outcomes.text: Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): advances in the treatment of disease; ethical issues of medical and other technologies.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): cloning; genetic modifications; modern communications systems.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): the individual in his/her surroundings; effect of environment on individuals; protest action to protect one’s locality; ways of contributing to environmental awareness.

Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): global warming; acid rain; air pollution; water pollution; noise pollution; destruction of rain forests; damage to animal world; solutions and cost implications.
Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): saving endangered species and landscapes.

topics.title: Contemporary aspects of the country/ies where Urdu is spoken

outcomes.text: Study, with reference to Urdu-speaking countries/communities (examples, not prescriptive): e.g. political, regional, social issues.
